author: Adeel Ahmad
title: Systems, AI & Security
intro: I'm a software engineer in Melbourne. This page is for people who have my CV and want to understand how the different parts of it connect.
description: A dated record of what Adeel Ahmad worked on and learned, across software, infrastructure, security and AI.

events.title: Getting into security
events.body: I started poking at networks and security in grade 8 in Lahore, long before my first software job.

events.title: First formal vulnerability assessment
events.body: In 2006, while still at school, I did my first formal vulnerability assessment, on a company's website, and found issues that would have let attackers in. The company's CEO later wrote me a recommendation letter.

events.title: Computer-science education
events.body: Studied computer science at the Institute of Management Sciences in Lahore while working.

events.title: APTLOGIX: application development and integration
events.body: My first professional role included CMS and e-commerce development, C#/.NET backends and third-party integrations.

events.title: Senior Software Engineer at PureLogics
events.body: Worked as a senior software engineer before taking on a wider technical role.

events.title: PureLogics: co-partner and CTO
events.body: Kept developing while also looking after network security and the company's systems.

events.title: Virtualization, networks and telephony
events.body: Worked with VMware, Asterisk and Cisco networking. My later virtualization work progressed through XenServer and then Proxmox/KVM; these were successive stages, not one simultaneous deployment.
events.note: These came one after another; I don't have exact start dates.

events.title: A Facebook-integrated application
events.body: Worked on a community application that integrated with Facebook's APIs.

events.title: Enterprise workflow automation
events.body: Built tools to automate quality-assurance workflows for a business.

events.title: Co-founded Geeks Chicago
events.body: Co-founded a small consultancy and worked on client projects and solution design.

events.title: Xoho Tech: founder and CTO
events.body: Ran a consultancy that grew to about 40 people across Pakistan and the United States. I wrote code, designed systems, handled security and delivery, and did the sales.

events.title: Starting with AWS
events.body: AWS became part of our client work early on, around 2013.

events.title: Digital archives and video platforms
events.body: Worked on AWS-hosted archive and video-streaming systems with searchable collections.

events.title: Institutional archival management
events.body: Delivered archival-management and audiovisual-platform work involving data modeling, media integration, search and maintainable application architecture.

events.title: Tools for archival quality and integrity
events.body: Worked on multiple applications for collection management, data quality and file integrity within an archival-software portfolio.

events.title: E-signature application engineering
events.body: Contributed to an AWS-hosted e-signature application, including workflow design and enterprise integration.

events.title: Writing down our engineering practices
events.body: Wrote the company's engineering guide: cloud practices, identity, secure coding, style and onboarding.

events.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate
events.body: My first AWS certification.

events.title: Power cuts became a developer problem
events.body: Power cuts kept interrupting work and sometimes losing it. I started looking at hosting development environments remotely so work would survive an outage.

events.title: Taking the browser IDE apart
events.body: Investigated the separation between the editor interface, extension host and background services, then used browser-hosted VS Code tooling in later remote-development iterations.

events.title: A home lab to learn the layers underneath
events.body: Built a small Proxmox, Ceph and ZFS cluster at home to understand storage and virtualisation properly.

events.title: Shared, template-based development environments
events.body: Built Linux-container templates with project dependencies and browser-based editing on a rented European server. Private networking, cloning and shared resources made the environment reusable across developers.

events.title: Request-driven workspace shutdown and wake-up
events.body: Used a web server and shell scripts to stop idle workspaces and restart them when a browser request arrived, rather than keeping every development environment running continuously.

events.title: Experimented with Firecracker developer environments
events.body: Moved from container-based workspace experiments toward Firecracker microVMs, exploring the balance between isolation, resource use and lightweight startup.

events.title: Teaching containers and systems thinking
events.body: Taught the team containers and some of the infrastructure under our applications.

events.title: Workspaces as an onboarding and continuity system
events.body: Used persistent editor state, snapshots, cloneable environments and preinstalled dependencies to support handovers, onboarding and returning to an existing project.

events.title: Media-monitoring platform work
events.body: Worked on systems that collect, search and monitor media content.

events.title: Planning an open platform for audiovisual metadata
events.body: I was on the core team planning an open platform that uses speech recognition, OCR and other machine learning to describe large audiovisual archives. In September 2017 we spent three days on requirements, comparing candidate tools for each part of the pipeline and sketching workflows. The plan was presented at the AMIA conference that December.
events.evidence: Workshop notes, September 2017, and public project documentation

events.title: Access to OpenAI's API beta
events.body: Got access to OpenAI's private API beta while running the consultancy, and started experimenting with it.
events.note: This is the date access was granted.

events.title: Researching browser-based compute and developer tooling
events.body: Explored browser extensions, React internals, WebRTC desktop access, cloud isolation and customizable developer environments.

events.title: Cevo: AWS cloud consulting
events.body: Moved into cloud consulting in Australia, working across solution architecture, application integration and technical delivery.

events.title: Cloud API delivery and domain-team leadership
events.body: Built cloud APIs and integrations, including Consumer Data Right services, and led the engineers working on them.

events.title: Enterprise retrieval and permission-aware knowledge access
events.body: Worked on enterprise retrieval involving Amazon Q Business and SharePoint, with attention to access-aware search rather than treating all content as equally available.

events.title: Document and email processing pipelines
events.body: Worked with data transformation, machine learning and language-model components in document and email-processing workflows.

events.title: WebRTC beyond the browser IDE
events.body: Experimented with browser-delivered desktops where an editor and shell were not enough for development or QA, considering bandwidth, frame rate, audio and client requirements.

events.title: Explaining LLMs and Transformers
events.body: Prepared presentation material on Transformers, attention, fine-tuning, prompts, agents and plugins.

events.title: Writing about open language models
events.body: Discussed the possibilities of open LLMs and Falcon, reflecting an active interest in models that could be adapted and run beyond a single managed service.

events.title: The development environment is part of DevOps
events.body: Outlined development environments as versioned, reproducible artifacts: dependency definitions, prebuilds and consistent tooling belong in the delivery process, not in a separate manual setup guide.

events.title: Separate the IDE from the application runtime
events.body: Explored a multi-container workspace design with separate responsibilities for the editor and the application, considering managed orchestration where appropriate.

events.title: Built workspace images with GitLab CI/CD
events.body: Adapted an existing workspace base image, added project dependencies in a Dockerfile and arranged automated environment builds on change.

events.title: Developer portals as a shared starting point
events.body: Proposed an internal developer portal for APIs, docs, examples and environment setup. Backstage was one option I looked at.

events.title: Treating extension distribution as an architecture constraint
events.body: Considered how custom IDE distributions, extension marketplaces and distribution terms affect the viability of a developer-platform design.

events.title: Managed workspaces, data locality and client independence
events.body: Explored keeping development near shared services, controlling dependency access centrally and separating the developer’s access device from the hosted workspace.

events.title: Private AI coding assistance and the adoption problem
events.body: Proposed integrating privately hosted model endpoints into developer environments. The design considered both code confidentiality and the risk of useful tools being adopted outside sanctioned workflows.

events.title: Jira-triggered AI preparation before a developer starts
events.body: Outlined a workflow in which a task triggers an ephemeral development environment and an AI system prepares a plan and carries out preliminary work before the engineer takes over.
events.note: This was a proposal. It wasn't built as a whole.

events.title: Visible plans, action records and human verification
events.body: The engineer would see what the AI planned and what it actually did, verify the work and retain responsibility for the result. This put inspectability and handoff into the workflow design.

events.title: Runnable environments for pull-request review
events.body: Proposed opening a pull request into a checked-out, running browser workspace so a reviewer could examine behavior as well as code before accepting a change.

events.title: Scope, supportability and a runnable pilot
events.body: Worked through the operational cost and training implications of a developer-platform proposal, favouring a small, understandable pilot with runnable examples over an all-at-once platform build.

events.title: Sharing the remote-development journey
events.body: Gave a talk on how our setup went from hosted workspaces to containers, prebuilt environments and AI-assisted workflows.

events.title: Second Brain: owned knowledge and adaptable consumption
events.body: Explored a personal-knowledge system that retains source material, retrieves relevant context and adapts outputs to how a person consumes information, including audio.
events.note: I don't have the exact date of the talk.

events.title: Small, domain-specific models on consumer hardware
events.body: Reported experiments adapting small GPT-NeoX models for a focused task such as email drafting, with local execution on consumer hardware.

events.title: Article-to-podcast workflow in Python
events.body: Built a script that transformed source content into podcast-style text and used the macOS speech tooling to produce an audio output.

events.title: Browser-to-podcast automation with Shortcuts
events.body: Shared an iOS/macOS Shortcut for turning browser content into podcast-style output, making the workflow usable beyond a development shell.

events.title: Thinking about small-model serving economics
events.body: Proposed serving approaches that account for idle workloads and the cost of keeping a model resident in memory.

events.title: Local and edge AI as an architectural choice
events.body: Wrote about running smaller models closer to the data, for privacy and cost reasons.

events.title: A multi-agent AutoGen prototype
events.body: Built a GPT-4 and AutoGen notebook with roles such as account manager, architect, critic and engineer, with a person approving the plan before code ran.

events.title: Knowledge graphs, vector search and RAG together
events.body: Argued that graph structure and vector search work better together than vector search alone.

events.title: Prompt and SQL-injection risks in AI applications
events.body: Raised injection concerns in an AI-assisted data-access approach, including the importance of how untrusted input reaches templates and tools.

events.title: Private, multi-model agent orchestration
events.body: Discussed AutoGen and Griptape as options for composing multi-model agents, including the use of private or open models.

events.title: Adaptive decoys as an AI-security idea
events.body: Proposed investigating whether language models could make controlled decoy environments more realistic and useful for studying attacker behavior.

events.title: Structured metadata for retrieval
events.body: Wrote about RDF and metadata as part of the relationship between language models, data semantics and information retrieval.

events.title: Local supervised fine-tuning
events.body: Ran local fine-tuning experiments using llama.cpp and Llama/OpenChat-class models, working through training data, adaptation and evaluation.

events.title: Synthetic data, fine-tuning and quantization loops
events.body: Explored a cyclic workflow in which models help generate and refine task-focused training data before further fine-tuning and quantization.

events.title: Writing up AI-prepared developer workspaces
events.body: Published a design for a model to plan and prepare isolated development work after requirements and Jira tasks are defined, leaving final code ownership and review with the engineer.

events.title: Personal assistants and audio knowledge workflows
events.body: Outlined personal-assistant workflows that combine open tooling, automation, knowledge distillation and customized written or audio briefings.

events.title: Structured reasoning with smaller models
events.body: Experimented with situation, task, action and result structures to guide agent work and reflection with quantized models.

events.title: Training data with explicit reasoning and protection structure
events.body: Tried building fine-tuning data that spells out the reasoning steps, including steps meant to resist misuse.

events.title: Model behavior and serialization risk
events.body: Raised questions about model interaction with serialized or binary representations as part of broader AI-security exploration.

events.title: Policy-as-code exploration with Cedar
events.body: Discussed experiments with Cedar and the problem of managing security policy at scale.

events.title: Exploring smaller-model inference in serverless environments
events.body: Discussed ONNX and the possibility of fitting small-model inference into serverless execution models.

events.title: Separating cloud-platform security from AI-application security
events.body: Wrote about security gaps that remain at the application layer even when the underlying AI platform provides security controls.

events.title: AWS Solutions Architect Professional
events.body: Passed the AWS Solutions Architect Professional exam.

events.title: Snowflake SnowPro Core
events.body: Passed the SnowPro Core exam while working on data platforms.

events.title: Lyrebird Health: tech lead on a clinical AI product
events.body: Tech lead on a clinical AI product, covering the AWS setup, AI engineering and security.

events.title: Clinical AI: evaluation, provenance and security
events.body: Worked on clinical language-model applications with attention to structured extraction, evaluation, prompt versioning, provenance and protection of sensitive data.

events.title: Early voice-AI evaluation
events.body: Took part in early testing of a voice AI product, which got me into realtime and streaming systems.

events.title: Responsible-disclosure work in AI systems
events.body: Worked on AI-system security research and submitted a vulnerability report through a responsible-disclosure channel.

events.title: Prompt experiments with reasoning models
events.body: Shared an observation from experimenting with reward-oriented wording in reasoning-model prompts.

events.title: Commonwealth Bank: Staff Platform Engineer
events.body: Joined Commonwealth Bank's AI Acceleration squad, working on applied AI from design to production.

events.title: Applied-AI delivery from early design to production
events.body: Work across development, data and infrastructure to get AI applications from design into production.

events.title: Identity and authorization for AI applications
events.body: Worked on identity and authorization patterns for service-to-service and agent-to-tool interactions, with attention to least privilege and avoiding shared secrets.

events.title: Researching small-model reasoning with RL and SFT
events.body: Wrote publicly about using reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning to study reasoning in small models.

events.title: AI-application security evaluation
events.body: Carried out hands-on AI-application security evaluation, considering the boundary between language-model output and application behavior.

events.title: Comparative audio-intelligence prototyping
events.body: Built a prototype to compare audio-analysis approaches, exploring speaker separation, timestamps and contextual interaction.

events.title: Writing about capability and agent risk
events.body: Discussed the security implications of increasingly capable models and agents, including the trade-offs of smaller task-specific models.

events.title: An AI hackathon team
events.body: Led a team at an internal AI hackathon, from the problem to a working demo.

events.title: Mentoring, standards and engineering delivery
events.body: Combined hands-on engineering with technical guidance, design discussions, mentoring and efforts to improve delivery practices.

events.title: Security Champion
events.body: Took on the Security Champion role for my squad.

events.title: Declarative agents and filesystem-native tools
events.body: Proposed composing agents from explicit declarations and making tools discoverable through familiar filesystem and command-line interfaces.

events.title: Expert scaffolding and model adaptation
events.body: Investigated how small models learn with reasoning scaffolds and examined internal differences between base and adapted models.

events.title: Testing what model adaptation preserves and changes
events.body: Shared experimental observations about internal representations after fine-tuning and proposed testing whether those observations generalize across model families.

events.title: Latent Contextual Reinforcement
events.body: Wrote up a research idea about guiding small models to reason better without retraining all of their weights.

events.title: Completion proxy with an agent-tool runtime
events.body: Developed a single-binary Go proxy concept that exposes a chat-completions-compatible interface and separates model backends from tool registry and execution responsibilities.

events.title: JuiceFS fork: storage, caching and backend engineering
events.body: Working in a JuiceFS fork on storage backends, caching, replication, integrity and block access.
events.note: This is work in my fork, not an upstream JuiceFS release.

events.title: MLX model-inspection and comparison tools
events.body: Developed tooling for layer-wise predictions, activation comparisons, geometric drift, ablation-style investigation and inspectable CLI/TUI output.

events.title: A lesson in parallel-agent integration
events.body: A multi-agent development effort exposed the cost of starting dependent implementation before the shared interface was settled. The resulting lesson was to establish and verify the common contract before composing dependent work.

events.title: CTXConfig: choose context at the symbol level
events.body: Explored AST-aware context selection and task planning around source symbols, rather than treating entire repositories as undifferentiated model input.

events.title: agentic-agile: test-driven agent workflows
events.body: Published a Claude Code plugin organized around human-gated planning, test-first work, review stages and explicit completion checks.

events.title: Measuring agent-assisted development
events.body: Reported on a development run using tokens, packages, tests, commits and sprint output to examine agent-assisted engineering beyond a simple completion claim.

events.title: Isolation as an explicit agent-runtime requirement
events.body: Explored packaged agents running in microVMs and compared isolation approaches against a consistent set of requirements.

events.title: AgentRC: writing down what an agent may do
events.body: Published a working draft for packaging agents with explicit model, tool and network requests that a platform can grant, narrow or reject before execution.

events.title: Reflecting on years of local-model experimentation
events.body: Connected earlier fastText and local-inference work with later model adaptation and defensive tool-design concerns.

events.title: rclone filesystem adapters and media integration
events.body: Built filesystem adapters in an rclone fork, including one for a media server. The upstream proposal was closed without merging.

events.title: Versioned work state, not just conversation history
events.body: Designed a state-document approach for preserving decisions, versions and task state across agent work, including an interactive view of changes over time.

events.title: Conversation and artifact preservation
events.body: Built browser-extension tooling aimed at preserving a user’s own conversations and generated artifacts as durable, inspectable records.

events.title: Local Python execution inside a document editor
events.body: Prototyped a browser extension that runs Python locally with Pyodide, so code examples in a document can run where they are written.

events.title: MLX reinforcement-learning and guided-training tooling
events.body: Developed training tooling for Apple Silicon, with configurable tasks, evaluators, rewards, supervised modes and guided reasoning experiments.

events.title: OpenWrt traffic-control fix merged upstream
events.body: Fixed bidirectional traffic shaping in luci-app-trafficctl, with tests. The pull request was merged upstream.

events.title: Out-of-band automation through PiKVM
events.body: Prototyped a hardware-control interface for recovery and machine administration when ordinary network access is unavailable.

events.title: Local GRPO and LoRA experiments on Apple Silicon
events.body: Kept training small models at home: guided-reasoning runs, quantisation and tooling to make runs repeatable.

events.title: ReqWall: portable policies, replaceable enforcement
events.body: Explored request-policy tooling in which the rules are durable and browser or router enforcement mechanisms can be replaced independently.

events.title: Reusable media-ingestion pipelines
events.body: Developed the foundation of a reusable pipeline for audio, video and image ingestion, indexing and search.

events.title: Android administration and feasibility testing
events.body: Worked through device-management feasibility and repeatable ADB/Shizuku startup, distinguishing a practical administration path from unsupported assumptions about device access.

events.title: agent-handoff: durable decisions across sessions
events.body: Published a tool for preserving settled decisions, open work and versioned handoff state between AI sessions rather than repeatedly reconstructing context.

events.title: Snapback: browse backup history without replacing live data
events.body: Defined a Linux/macOS tool for read-only, per-directory historical views and copy-back restoration, built around the constraint that the live filesystem must never be over-mounted.

events.title: aloop: evolving the agentic-agile workflow
events.body: Reframed the workflow around test-driven agents, review waves, a final gate and explicit handoff state between cleared contexts.

events.title: Workstation recovery and GPU diagnostics
events.body: Worked through memory compatibility, firmware settings, storage and network hardware, Linux drivers and GPU recovery on an older workstation platform.

events.title: Browser storage and execution-context debugging
events.body: Worked on IndexedDB export and the differences between browser, extension and worker contexts when expected DOM or URL facilities were unavailable.

events.title: Wireless backhaul and OpenWrt diagnostics
events.body: Investigated home wireless-backhaul constraints, routing and bridging behavior, TCP settings and radio state across a mixed-device network.

events.title: A writing project on AI application principles
events.body: Began shaping a writing project about repeatable architecture, governance and operating principles for AI applications.

events.title: USB-device emulation on Raspberry Pi
events.body: Explored a Raspberry Pi Zero starting point for a USB-device-emulation prototype and the possibility of later portability.

events.title: Privacy questions in voice-AI pipelines
events.body: Examined voice-AI security questions including how personally identifiable information could be handled in streaming and voice-token pipelines.

events.title: anytopdf: an extensible path from media to searchable documents
events.body: Designed an extensible document pipeline for files, images, audio and video, including transcripts, captions and keyframe metadata, with Python work and a longer-term Rust architecture.

events.title: Lens product identity and interface design
events.body: Worked on the look and interface for Lens across web, app and command line.

events.title: Lens: a private, user-owned AI hub
events.body: Planned a private AI hub that runs on my own machines: my notes and files, searchable, with answers that cite sources and actions that need my approval.

events.title: Putting this record together
events.body: Put this timeline together to show how the work connects.

events.title: Security research at execution boundaries
events.body: Investigated AI execution environments and sandbox boundaries through protocol and systems analysis, while keeping target-specific and undisclosed research separate from the public record.

events.title: Speech recognition, OCR and visual-media processing
events.body: Worked with speech-recognition, OCR and media-processing tools before the later LLM-focused projects.

events.title: Telephony and realtime communication
events.body: Worked across Asterisk, FreePBX and later telephony systems, including audio codecs, recording, SMS integration and realtime browser communication.

events.title: Routing, VPNs and identity-aware access
events.body: Built experience across switching, routing, firewalls, overlay networking, VPNs and identity-aware access. Tool adoption spans different periods rather than a single first-use date.

events.title: MacPilot: natural-language desktop automation
events.body: Experimented with model-driven macOS control using accessibility interfaces, AppleScript, OCR and asynchronous orchestration.

method.scope: This is a selection, not everything. Work for employers and clients is described in general terms, without client names or internal details.
method.evidence: Some entries link to public posts or code. The rest come from my own notes and records.
method.dates: Some dates are exact and some are approximate. Approximate ones say so.
method.skills: Skill tags show what a piece of work involved. They are not ratings.
method.research: Experiments and proposals are labelled as such. Not everything here was finished or went into production.
method.personal: These are my own views, not my employer's.
